payload.claim: No test ever calls `faults` twice with diverging `parsed` outcomes, so `_record`'s preference for the newest *parsed* text over a later unparsed one is never exercised. `test_a_draft_with_faults_goes_back_to_the_same_session_naming_each_line` always has both faults() calls return `parsed=True`, and `test_a_failed_send_back_keeps_the_last_draft_that_parsed_and_says_why` only ever calls `faults` once (every failure mode it drives aborts the send-back before a second `faults(new_text)` call is reached), so `newest_parsed` is only ever set from a single candidate in every test. Deleting the `if outcome.parsed:` guard so `newest_parsed = candidate` runs unconditionally makes the session return whatever text a later, unparseable send-back produced instead of falling back to the last text that did parse, exactly the regression criterion 1's 'a returned text that does not parse ... with and without an earlier one that did' clause and criterion 3 require the suite to catch, and the full suite stays green under that edit.
